detection.statement: A frozen board predicate identifies positions in which exactly one opponent non-pawn piece is legally capturable and has zero geometric defenders.
detection.evidence: 20.4% of 57,504 classifiable positions sampled from 60,000 unfiltered rated Lichess games (2013-01); 22.5% of 77,978 classifiable Lichess puzzle positions.
detection.robustness: 0.64% of T+ items flip to 'defended' under the Lichess ray-defence definition of is_defended.

recording.statement: Whether the player's move captured the designated target is recordable from the position and the move alone, with no engine, no result and no post-reveal information.
recording.evidence: research/measurement/predicates.py::observed_action; negative-controls.ts::outcomeLeakControl asserts an identical table after stripping every oracle field.

task_level_scoring.statement: Hit rate, false-alarm rate, sensitivity d' and response criterion c are computable for an item set under published formulae.
task_level_scoring.evidence: Stanislaw & Todorov (1999) with the Hautus (1995) loglinear correction; cross-language equivalence pinned by tests/research/measurement-sdt.test.ts.

second_iteration_rule_class_search.answer: yes for exactly one of five candidates tried

permitted.statement: In a corpus of 60,000 unfiltered rated games, the rule 'if the opponent threatens mate next move, play a move that stops it' prescribes an action that is Stockfish's own best move on 96.8% of trigger-positive items, and on 100.0% of the items where the rule prescribes anything at all; the same action is the engine's best on 20.0% of trigger-negative items.

still_not_permitted.statement_refuted_or_unresolved: that RC-06 is ready for a human pilot
still_not_permitted.why: T+ and T- differ by max |SMD| 0.573, so the item-difficulty confound of the first iteration applies unchanged; the base rate is 1.24% of not-in-check positions; and a multiple-baseline design needs three independently measurable rule classes where there is one.

second_iteration_rule_class_search.mechanism: An offensive rule competes with the whole rest of the board and is wrong whenever something better exists. A defensive rule against mate has no competition, because the alternative is losing. Severity protects the prescription, and that is why the four capture-family candidates scored below the refuted incumbent.
corrections_to_the_first_iteration: F10 read the incumbent's non-monotone player d' as a defect of that rule class. The CEILING anchor's d' is also non-monotone (1.946, 2.040, 2.187, 2.085) at prescriptive validity 1.000, so non-monotonicity is not diagnostic.

ITEM_BANK_PROTOCOL rejected the recapture family because T reads a prior move. That was too strict -- history before the player's turn is available before behaviour -- and recapture was measured, then failed on its merits (B_valid|T+ = 0.660).
GO_NO_GO section 7 proposed an item-bank adjudication study as the next step. The owner overrode it; the rule-class search ran instead.
second_iteration_rule_class_search.no_trade_off_claimed: Spearman(separation, max |SMD|) = 0.536, p = 0.215, n = 7. Not evidence. Recorded as a hypothesis, not a finding.
